title: Select: The Power of Extreme Criteria
coreMove: Replace soft approval with a high bar that rejects near-matches before they become commitments.
sourcePressure: The chapter closes exploration by turning discernment into harsh selection through minimum criteria, extreme criteria, and the 90 percent rule.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: A weak run would tell the reader to choose good opportunities more carefully without defining an extreme test.

exampleSpecs.domain: search-and-rescue team choosing one backpack drone before wildfire season
exampleSpecs.audience: team choosing under attractive vendor pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: good features are not enough without extreme criteria for field survival
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: They write minimum flight time and extreme wind criteria before watching vendor footage.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A drone spec sheet sits beside a wildfire map.

exampleSpecs.domain: historic lighthouse trust selecting a masonry contractor for one restoration season
exampleSpecs.stakes: pleasant bids must fail if they miss harsh preservation criteria
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: She scores each bid against salt-weather repair history and rejects the charming low bid.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Masonry bids lie beside a salt-stained brick sample.

exampleSpecs.domain: cybersecurity team selecting an incident-response retainer after a breach drill
exampleSpecs.audience: team tempted by polished sales decks
exampleSpecs.stakes: near-match vendors may fail the true crisis test
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: They ask each vendor to walk the breach-drill timeline and reject anyone below the 90 percent response bar.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A breach-drill timeline is clipped to vendor decks.

exampleSpecs.domain: independent perfumer choosing one formula for a restricted ingredient launch
exampleSpecs.stakes: extreme criteria prevent charm from becoming a weak launch
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Before, she loves five samples; after, only the formula passing wear, cost, and restriction criteria remains.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Five scent strips fan beside an ingredient restriction sheet.

exampleSpecs.domain: regional chess league selecting a finals venue for wheelchair access and broadcast reliability
exampleSpecs.stakes: criteria must reject attractive rooms that fail core access or broadcast needs
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: He reviews the previous venue complaint beside the new venue grid and writes nonnegotiable access plus signal tests.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A venue grid sits beside an access complaint letter.

exampleSpecs.domain: archaeology field director choosing one dig square before monsoon permits expire
exampleSpecs.audience: field director unable to chase every promising square
exampleSpecs.stakes: extreme criteria protect scarce permit days
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The most photogenic square fails the permit-days test; a duller grid wins because it can answer the dating question.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: A dig-square map is weighted by a permit folder.
